material.commit_comment: hub destroy keeps an unattached peer until its end and close are delivered; late attach is kept while the host holds the payload. Silent loss after the payload is released is tracked separately.
material.subject: Virtual hub defect found by the network bridge (dispatch 1792021026343-69-6335ed3eb92f4c3b, informational race probe, observed): a guest that destroys a connection right after connect leaves the host listener's Node peer with neither end nor close (Node accepted 1 connection, saw_end=false, saw_close=false). Cause (code read in network/virtual/hub.ts and net.ts): hub.destroy() deletes the server-side record, so attach() returns early and the queued end and close are dropped; guest-accepted connections take the same path (net.ts attach is skipped when ownerOfConnection is undefined; not yet tested). Fix: deliver end and close before the record is deleted, then witness both directions with a guest that destroys immediately after connect and with a guest server that accepts and immediately ends. This affects TLS and HTTP/2 teardown, so it precedes owc-tls-functional and owc-http2-supported sign-off.

material.commit_comment: TLS 1.3 in the guest: tls and https over the in-container engine; RFC 8448 traces; Node 24.15 interop in both directions; server cipher preference; ALPN and SNI; certificate chain and hostname verification; passphrase-protected keys are refused by design
material.subject: TLS functional in the OWC runtime: tls.connect, tls.createServer, tls.createSecureContext from PEM cert and key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 RSA, SEC1 EC), SNI, ALPN, certificate chain verification against the ca option, hostname verification, TLSSocket events and getters (getPeerCertificate, getProtocol, getCipher, alpnProtocol, authorized), and https client and server on top. Protocol: TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446) with TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256; X25519 and secp256r1 key shares; ECDSA P-256 and RSA-PSS and RSA-PKCS1 certificates. Witness: RFC 8448 handshake traces reproduce byte for byte; interop with Node 24.15 tls both directions through the scratch bridge harness; loopback in-container tests. Out of scope unless added and witnessed: TLS 1.2, system trust store (the browser has none; the ca option is required for verification), session resumption. Crypto primitives: host capabilities over @noble/hashes plus @noble/curves and @noble/ciphers (new dependencies: supply-chain scan required); RSA via BigInt in the host capability.

material.commit_comment: guest URL: a base path ending in '/' names a directory, so a relative reference resolves inside it (with dot segments normalised) instead of one level too high
material.subject: The guest URL resolves a relative reference one directory too high when the base path ends in '/': new URL('package.json','file:///work/node_modules/sodium-native/') gave file:///work/node_modules/package.json instead of file:///work/node_modules/sodium-native/package.json. resolveAgainst used path.dirname(base.pathname), which drops the trailing slash. Found by the sodium shim builder: require('sodium-native') failed in the container because require-addon read a missing package.json and reported 'Cannot find addon'. Fix: append inside the base path when it ends in '/', normalising dot segments.

material.commit_comment: CommonJS modules are compiled by the host with their file name, so stack frames carry a path instead of '<input>'; packages that locate their binary from a stack frame (bindings, and what is built on it) now resolve
material.subject: CommonJS modules appear in guest stack traces as '<input>', so packages that locate their binary from a stack frame cannot resolve it. bindings 1.5.0 getFileName() parses Error.stack, gets no path, and throws 'cannot read property indexOf of undefined'. Blocks require('better-sqlite3') (measured 2026-10-15: corpus entry better-sqlite3-native still RUNTIME_ERROR though its shim is integrated and verified 92/92 one level down). Fix: give CommonJS modules a real filename in stack traces, or handle the bindings package explicitly; prefer the general fix because it improves every stack trace and error message. Note the related owc-url-trailing-slash defect was fixed separately and did NOT resolve this one.
material.witness: packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/host-bridge.ts (new host.compileCjs) and runtime/guest/loader.ts (compileCjsWrapper passes the filename). Measured root cause: this QuickJS build names eval'd code '<input>' and ignores //# sourceURL, and globals.ts maps that name to undefined, so bindings 1.5.0 getFileName() read undefined and called undefined.indexOf. Live witness in this dispatch: better-sqlite3 11.5.0 through require('better-sqlite3') in the container prints '5', identical to the Node reference. The 148-entry corpus moved from 140 to 141 PASS with no other change.

material.commit_comment: QUIC connection grows MAX_STREAMS: a credit returns when a peer stream closes, MAX_STREAMS is queued and retransmitted on loss, with a STREAMS_BLOCKED valve
material.subject: The stage 2 QUIC connection does not grow MAX_STREAMS, so an OWC HTTP/3 server answers only about 128 sequential requests on one connection (128 of 130 measured by the stage 3 builder). Real clients send more requests per connection. Stage 4 scope (stream limits and flow control). Witness: 300 sequential requests on one connection to the container server, from aioquic, with every response correct; a second witness for the container client to aioquic. Found in the stage 3 build (finding L1).
material.witness: src/network/quic/connection.ts: mutable localMaxStreamsBidi and localMaxStreamsUni, a +1 credit when a peer stream closes both directions (RFC 9000 4.6 and 19.11), MAX_STREAMS queued as a max_streams record so loss retransmits it, STREAMS_BLOCKED as a safety valve, and the streams event unblocking the H3 client queue. Before: 128 of 300 sequential requests, failing at index 128 with a global timeout. After, measured by an independent verifier and re-run here: 300 of 300 and 1000 of 1000 sequential GETs byte-exact, 300 byte-exact at 2 percent loss, 500 concurrent; MAX_STREAMS on the wire grows 129 to 428 for n=300 and 129 to 1128 for n=1000, with credit exactly N. A credit-leak attack (200 streams opened and never closed) holds the limit at 128 and over-grants nothing.

material.commit_comment: HTTP/3 client close now reaches the peer: session close no longer waits for stream teardown, with a grace period after GOAWAY and a retry if the flush guard swallows the close
material.subject: The container's HTTP/3 client close() does not reach the peer: the session closes locally with code 256 but aioquic 1.6.1 records no ConnectionTerminated across two runs in a 14 s window. Server close is correct (GOAWAY then CONNECTION_CLOSE 256, seen by the peer). Found by the stage 3 verifier, repro /tmp/owc-r4/verify-h3/repro-1 (expected: grep ConnectionTerminated -> 0 matches). Decide whether the client must flush its CONNECTION_CLOSE before the socket closes, and witness it against aioquic.
material.witness: src/network/quic/h3-connection.ts: Http3Connection.busyCount replaces requestCount in maybeFinishClose so close no longer waits for Duplex teardown; a 1500 ms grace after GOAWAY; QuicConnection.close retries through scheduleFlush when the flushing guard swallows it. Before: the aioquic peer recorded no ConnectionTerminated across three runs while the guest reported a local code 256. After, measured by an independent verifier and re-run here: the peer observes ConnectionTerminated with error_code 256 at five of five call sites (immediate, after open, in flight, twice, and inside the data callback with 4 KiB queued) and while gracefully closing during a streaming response; the connection_close frame appears in the peer's received qlog, and 256 still arrives at 10 percent loss. destroy(undefined, 256) gives 256 immediately; destroy(Error('boom')) gives 258 plus the message, matching Node.

material.commit_comment: HTTP/3 over QUIC v1 with a static-table QPACK, plus congestion control, pacing and loss recovery
material.subject: HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) over QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000, transport; RFC 9001, TLS 1.3 integration and packet protection) with QPACK (RFC 9204), client and server over the virtual UDP hub, including packet number spaces, header protection, ACK ranges, STREAM and CRYPTO frames, flow control, loss detection and PTO timers, connection IDs, idle timeout, and CONNECTION_CLOSE. Node 24.15 has no QUIC or HTTP/3 module (node:quic and node:http3 are unknown with and without --experimental-quic), so the references are: RFC 9001 Appendix A packet protection and initial-secret vectors, and aioquic 1.6.1 (installed in the scratch venv /tmp/owc-r4/quic-ref/venv) interop both directions through the bridge harness. Depends on owc-tls-functional (TLS 1.3 handshake in QUIC mode) and the UDP path of the bridge. Witness plan is staged: transport and packet protection vectors first, then handshake interop, then HTTP/3 request and response with QPACK static table, then streams and flow control under loss.
material.witness: src/network/quic: transport and packet protection, the TLS 1.3 handshake in QUIC mode, connection.ts, recovery.ts, h3-connection.ts, h3-api.ts and the QPACK codec. An independent adversarial verifier, re-run here, reports zero failures on all three previously open claims: 300 of 300 and 1000 of 1000 sequential requests with MAX_STREAMS growing on the wire and no credit leak; the peer observing the client's CONNECTION_CLOSE code 256 at five of five call sites including under 10 percent loss; and NewReno with pacing where a 2.5 second blackout yields ssthresh 2400 equal to the minimum window, the signature of RFC 9002 7.6.2, recovering afterwards and never collapsing. Eleven loss and reordering runs of 1 MiB each delivered byte-exact data across 0, 1, 5, 10 and 20 percent loss in each direction and 10 and 30 percent reordering. Handshake at 10 and 20 percent loss, key update with and without loss, idle timeout, a malformed frame giving 261 and header blocks up to 1.1 MB giving 263 all behave correctly. Not implemented and explicitly out of scope: 0-RTT, migration, ECN and stateless reset. Throughput of 70 to 260 KB/s is attributed to the send loop and bridge rather than congestion control and stays open as owc-guest-transport-throughput.

blocker_notes: Decision recorded, not made (session mcp-instruction-56080-1792097621879): npm install -g stays refused with 'Global installs are not supported by this runtime'. There is no global prefix in this container's file system and no bin directory on the default PATH to link into, so a global install would write nowhere a later command could find it; the default is to keep refusing rather than to invent one. Reversing it is a one-line change in npm/process.ts (install()) once a prefix is decided. npm run is implemented and witnessed; package-lock.json is written in lockfileVersion 3 layout, field-for-field identical to npm 11.12.1's own lockfile for the same manifest.

Global installs stay refused unless the user decides otherwise: that decision is recorded here, not made.

material.commit_comment: resolve owc-shell-globbing: pathname expansion witnessed against the host /bin/sh
material.subject: The shell performs no pathname expansion: 'echo *', 'echo *.txt', 'echo ?.txt' and 'echo [ac]*' print the literal patterns, and 'grep . *.txt' fails with ENOENT '/work/*.txt'. blocker_notes: DECISION (brotli and zstd), recorded before implementing: measured on 2026-10-16. Pure-JS brotli (npm 'brotli' 2.1.0) is 2.2 MB unpacked; brotli-wasm 3.0.1 is a 3.2 MB package carrying a WASM module; @bokuweb/zstd-wasm is 904 KB. fzstd 0.1.1 is 65 KB and pure JS but exports decompress only - no compress, so it cannot cover zstdCompressSync. Decision: brotli (both directions) and zstd compression go through the WebAssembly bridge (runtime/guest/wasm.ts) as codec modules, not as multi-megabyte JS inlined into the guest source; zstd decompression is deliberately not taken separately, so the codec arrives as one mechanism. Until the bridge carries them, zlib.brotli*/zstd* keep throwing ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. Follow-up row: owc-brotli-zstd-wasm.
material.subject: Ciphers and compression gaps (witness dispatch 1792020269182-7-9453f953e0e0f15b): crypto.createCipheriv with aes-128-cbc throws ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE (createHash sha256 and createHmac are equal to Node and are not in this row); brotliCompressSync and brotliDecompressSync and zstd round trips throw ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. Implement createCipheriv and createDecipheriv on top of @noble/ciphers (AES-CBC, AES-CTR, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 as available there) with Node's error codes for bad keys and IVs, witnessed against Node's crypto. Brotli and zstd are a separate decision (a pure-JS brotli decoder and encoder are large): record that decision here before implementing.

acceptance_criteria: npm install esbuild in the container exits 0 with a working esbuild, or refuses with one clear reason naming the platform binary it cannot run
No postinstall step leaves the tree in a half-installed state
The corpus entry esbuild-native moves off HOST_INSTALL or stays there with the refusal text recorded as the expected result
material.description: The corpus entry esbuild-native reports HOST_INSTALL: esbuild's npm postinstall runs the platform binary it shipped, which is a real executable and cannot run in the container. Either install the package without running that step (esbuild ships a js-install / ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH path) or make the install refuse with one clear line naming the binary, instead of failing inside a postinstall script the user never sees.
material.resolution: Refusal branch taken: esbuild ships no JavaScript or WebAssembly fallback, so it cannot work in a JavaScript-only container. packages/core/src/npm/native.ts finds the executable a package's platform dependency shipped (ELF/Mach-O/PE, skipping .node/.so/.dylib/.dll, which are loaded not executed), and packages/core/src/npm/installer.ts refuses the install script with ENOEXEC naming it, before the script runs. Live run: npm install esbuild exits 126 with 'npm error esbuild@0.24.2 runs the native executable /work/node_modules/@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild in its postinstall script; this container executes JavaScript only'; require('esbuild').transformSync still fails afterwards, as expected. Previous behaviour was a QuickJS abort (RuntimeError: null function or function signature mismatch) naming only 'node install.js'. core-js regression: install exit 0, postinstall runs, works.
material.title: esbuild npm install fails in its postinstall platform binary
material.witness: exec (bash dispatch): node tsx /tmp/owc-r4/probe2/run-owc-repo.mts /tmp/owc-r4/esb-base main.js 180000 -> [owc install exit 126] ... npm error code ENOEXEC / npm error path /work/node_modules/esbuild / npm error command sh -c node install.js / npm error esbuild@0.24.2 runs the native executable /work/node_modules/@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild in its postinstall script; this container executes JavaScript only / Process exited with code: 126; program output ESBUILD_FAIL (transformSync unusable)

material.commit_comment: guest: route an unhandled rejection to the domain that owns the promise, else to process unhandledRejection listeners, else end the process
material.subject: Async context and promise rejection gaps (witness dispatch 1792020333437-8-94a781f6aca1795d): AsyncLocalStorage keeps its store across setTimeout, promise then, nextTick and setImmediate but loses it across await (await null, await timer, await after a timer read undefined where Node keeps the store); unhandled promise rejection reporting absent (Node exits 1 at the rejection; OWC exits 0 and runs later timers). Classify each: fix in the guest if the engine exposes a hook (the QuickJS C API has JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker; check whether quickjs-emscripten 0.31 exposes it), otherwise ENGINE with the exact missing hook named as evidence.

acceptance_criteria: A single-quoted line containing parentheses runs in the playground terminal exactly as /bin/sh runs it
echo with a quoted ), (, |, ; and space each match the host on stdout, stderr and exit code
A node -e one-liner with parentheses typed into the playground terminal runs instead of reporting a syntax error
material.description: Typed into the playground's terminal (the interactive shell path, the one behind useShell with osc), a line whose single-quoted argument contains parentheses is mis-tokenized: `node -e 'console.log(typeof WebAssembly)'` reports "Error: syntax error near unexpected token ))))'" and the same shape failed for `echo ... >> /w.js` with `)))`. The same line fed through ShellProcess.executeCommand runs fine, so the defect is in the interactive line path, not in the command implementations. The host /bin/sh parses all of these correctly. Find where the interactive path splits on ) and make quoting win there.

material.description: Six known shell divergences still open, each small and independent: (1) unexpand -t with a comma-separated tab list diverges from the host; (2) timeout can never return 124, because the container's child processes have no signal delivery to time out; (3) zip --version is refused; (4) execSync('curl') fails honestly instead of running the curl implementation the shell already has; (5) ifconfig cannot list live hub state because CommandContext carries no network handle; (6) `lspci 2>/dev/null` fails with ENOENT '/dev' in the redirect path at root level, although /dev/null is meant to be a sink. Fix each that can be fixed, and for the rest write the reason into Readme.md so the behaviour is on the record rather than a surprise.

material.witness: Two-arm differential on HEAD 54e91e8cf627f8c5464f55456c1e3f924e5cdcb7. Arm A: real better-sqlite3@11.5.0 native add-on on host Node v24.15.0. material.description: Measured 2026-10-21: capability arguments are JSON, so every payload crosses the guest/host bridge as base64 text, and that is 31 of 46 ms per 64 KiB chunk — the ceiling is ~1 MiB/s. The guest base64 codec was the largest single term and is already fixed (commit 16279bf, throughput doubled to ~1.4 MiB/s TCP). What remains is the representation itself. Give the network and HTTP paths a binary channel: let the guest hand its bytes to the host as an ArrayBuffer (the bridge already has newArrayBuffer/getArrayBuffer, and the wasm bridge already retains handles), so net writes, net reads, HTTP request and response bodies, HTTP/2 DATA frames, undici and fetch move bytes without a base64 round trip.

material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: Asyncify suspend for sync capabilities
material.description: create-react-app's last mile calls spawnSync('npm', ['install', '--no-audit', '--save', 'web-vitals@^2.1.0']) and gets "ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED: child_process: the shell command npm install cannot run inside a synchronous call on this runtime; use the asynchronous API" — the same spec installed asynchronously adds 29 packages in 2.3 s, so the work is possible, only the synchronous form is refused. The guest runs on a quickjs-emscripten asyncify build and the container already has a synchronous pump (runToCompletionSync with sleepMs and a sync mode) that suspends the guest and resumes it later. So a synchronous capability that needs the host network can suspend the guest instead of refusing: guest code keeps its synchronous semantics while the host completes the work. Implement that for the sync child_process path (npm install, and the other commands currently refused), and prove it with create-react-app.
material.title: Synchronous capabilities that need the host network should suspend the guest, not refuse

material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: rocksdb-native routed to the shim
material.description: A program using hypercore with random-access-memory fails: "Cannot load addon 'file:///node_modules/rocksdb-native/prebuilds/linux-x64/rocksdb-native.node'" at require-addon/lib/node.js:37, reached from rocksdb-native -> hypercore-storage -> hypercore. The container already ships a JavaScript reimplementation of rocksdb 5.2.1 (packages/core/src/napi/rocksdb/index.ts), registered in packages/core/src/napi/registry.ts under the package name 'rocksdb' with the binary paths build/Release/rocksdb.node and build/Debug/rocksdb.node. Neither the package name 'rocksdb-native' nor a prebuilds/<platform>/<name>.node path is registered, so the load falls through to a real dlopen and fails. Route the newer package and its prebuild layout through the same registry, and if hypercore-storage needs more of the RocksDB surface than the shim has (column families, iterators with seek, snapshots), say so and find whether hypercore can be given random-access-memory instead, which is what the user actually wants.

acceptance_criteria: A program that requires hypercore with random-access-memory runs in the container, or fails with one clear line naming what is missing instead of a stack through require-addon

rocksdb-native (package) and a prebuilds/<platform>/<name>.node path resolve through the Node-API shim registry the way build/Release/<name>.node does, or the failure names the shim mechanism and lists what is registered
If hypercore-storage genuinely cannot run on the rocksdb shim, find whether it can be pointed at random-access-memory and make that path work
row.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: rocksdb-native routed to the shim
row.description: A program using hypercore with random-access-memory fails: "Cannot load addon 'file:///node_modules/rocksdb-native/prebuilds/linux-x64/rocksdb-native.node'" at require-addon/lib/node.js:37, reached from rocksdb-native -> hypercore-storage -> hypercore. The container already ships a JavaScript reimplementation of rocksdb 5.2.1 (packages/core/src/napi/rocksdb/index.ts), registered in packages/core/src/napi/registry.ts under the package name 'rocksdb' with the binary paths build/Release/rocksdb.node and build/Debug/rocksdb.node. Neither the package name 'rocksdb-native' nor a prebuilds/<platform>/<name>.node path is registered, so the load falls through to a real dlopen and fails. Route the newer package and its prebuild layout through the same registry, and if hypercore-storage needs more of the RocksDB surface than the shim has (column families, iterators with seek, snapshots), say so and find whether hypercore can be given random-access-memory instead, which is what the user actually wants.

acceptance_criteria: sql.js in the container returns the same rows as host Node 24.15 for a create/insert/select script
The cause is named: which call sql.js makes to read its .wasm, and why that call returns different bytes than fs.readFileSync of the same path
No regression in the 30-case WebAssembly witness
material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: writeFile accepts bytes
material.description: sql.js 1.15.1 fails at init in the container with 'failed to asynchronously prepare wasm: CompileError: WebAssembly.Module(): section (code 1, "Type") extends past end of the module (length 9396207, remaining bytes 765542) @+8'. The file itself is not the problem: /work/node_modules/sql.js/dist/sql-wasm.wasm is 684897 bytes with magic 0,97,115,109, byte-identical in size and checksum to the host's copy, and in the container `new WebAssembly.Module(fs.readFileSync(file))`, the Uint8Array form, a slice and a fresh copy all compile with 53 exports; a 64 KiB openSync+readSync loop with and without an explicit position also returns byte-identical data. So sql.js is obtaining its bytes through some other route (an async read, a fetch, an inline base64, or a different dist file) and getting garbage. Find that route and fix what is ours.
material.title: sql.js init fails on a CompileError although its .wasm on disk is intact and compiles directly

acceptance_criteria: chmod 755 f and fs.chmodSync('f', 0o755) change the mode the way the host does, and a later stat reports it
If the virtual filesystem has no mode bits, chmod reports that honestly instead of succeeding and doing nothing
No regression in the fs corpus cases
material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: chmod records real mode bits
material.description: Measured 2026-10-21 while auditing the Readme: in the container `chmod 755 f` and `fs.chmodSync('f', 0o755)` both succeed and change nothing — `stat -c %a` stays 644 where the host prints 755. A no-op that reports success is worse than a refusal: a script that chmods and then relies on the mode silently gets the wrong behaviour. Either the virtual filesystem grows real mode bits, or chmod refuses with one clear line.

material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: compound lines register a background job
material.subject: packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts
material.summary: Blocked outside child.ts. `if true; then echo a & jobs; fi` prints only `a` where host /bin/sh prints `[1]+  Running                 echo a &` then `a`; `for i in 1; do echo a & jobs; done` likewise. Cause: the parser in builtins.ts drops a lone `&` (around its command-list loop, `// a background job; this shell has none, so the `&` is dropped`), so the engine never starts one and the job table stays empty. What is needed there: give the pipeline/command-list node a `background` flag and have the engine call a host-installed starter when it runs one. Two shapes fit the module: add an optional `startJob(text: string): void` to ShellState that the engine calls (child.ts installs one that parses `text` into its own stages and returns `[N] pid`), or import an exported `startBackgroundJob` from the dispatcher and wire it into the installed runner. Everything downstream already works off the one shared table - jobsBuiltin, waitBuiltin and runPendingJob read `state.jobs`, which is the host's own table through `state.host` - so only the registration is missing. Witness: /tmp/owc-r4/fix-jobctl/after.txt cases 11 and 16.
material.title: Compound lines register no background job: the script engine's parser drops `&`
material.witness: commit a7194f23b9d6ce1788a789813ffe4171c1ff16d5 in main history; the fix is present at HEAD and the bug is gone: an exhaustive grep (exhaustive: true, 196 files, 93078 lines) for the literal "command.t !== 'simple'" over packages/core/src returns 0 hits -- startBackgroundNode (builtins.ts:2326) no longer refuses a compound line, so '{ echo a; } &' and 'for ..; done &' register a job.

material.commit_comment: fix present at HEAD: bash job-control messages in child.ts
material.subject: packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/capabilities/child.ts
material.summary: Five measured deltas between the container shell and host /bin/sh for `&` job control, all in child.ts. Fixed: (1) `jobs` column layout delegated to the builtin's own jobsBuiltin (two spaces after the job marker, no ` &` on a Done job); (2) a job is reaped once `wait` has run it or the line's flush has, so a later `jobs` prints nothing; (3) `$(jobs)` no longer captures the pending job's output - runSubstitution now defers the pending-job flush to the line around it; (4) `exit` in a background segment no longer aborts the foreground line. Not fixed, blocked on another lane's file: (5) compound lines (`if true; then echo a & jobs; fi`) register no job because builtins.ts's parser drops `&` - it needs a `startJob(text)` callback on ShellState or an exported startBackgroundJob wired into its engine's runner. Delta 6 (`echo hi & echo done` prints `[1] N / done / hi` where bash may print `hi` first) is documented as a difference: jobs are run deferred, after the line's foreground, on a host that runs one command at a time.
material.title: Shell job control in child.ts: match bash for `&`, `jobs`, `wait`
material.witness: commit a7194f23b9d6ce1788a789813ffe4171c1ff16d5 in main history; fix present at HEAD: packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/capabilities/child.ts:2439 stderr += `wait: pid ${arg} is not a child of this shell\n` -- child.ts answers wait/jobs/`$!` with bash's own diagnostics ('no such job', 'not a pid or valid job spec'), and '&' prints nothing off an interactive line.

material.acceptance_criteria: import('./m.mjs?x=1') and import('./m.mjs') are two module instances; import.meta.url in each carries the query or fragment exactly as Node prints it; a module whose file name legitimately contains '?' or '#' still loads.
material.description: Now that a query or fragment resolves (row owc-esm-query-specifier), Node 24.15 still keeps it in the module's identity: import('./m.mjs?x=1') loads a DIFFERENT module instance than import('./m.mjs'), and import.meta.url inside it is 'file:///app/m.mjs?x=1'. OWC resolves to the bare path, so both imports share one instance and import.meta.url is 'file:///app/m.mjs'. Witnessed in the round-5 differential, .gm/exec-spool/out/bash-verify-owc-esm-query-specifier-88006-1792558908676-280.txt lines 19-23 (container) vs 6-9 (host): ./m.mjs?x=1, ./m.mjs?x=2 and ./m.mjs#frag all print url file:///app/m.mjs where the host prints the suffix. The suffix would have to survive resolution into the module name and be stripped only where the file is read (loadModule, isESM, readSource) and encoded by fileUrlOf/toFileUrl as a real search and fragment rather than %3F and %23.
material.subject: An ESM specifier's query or fragment is dropped from import.meta.url and from module identity
material.witness: host v24.15.0 vs container, identical stdout and exit 0: ./m.mjs, ?x=1, ?x=2, #frag, ?x=1#frag each print their own url, ./q%3F1.mjs and ./h%231.mjs load, distinct-instance true, meta.resolve file:///app/m.mjs?x=1. material.description: Found while re-running the verifier gap probe (witness .gm/witness-out/owc-verifier-open-gaps.txt): typeof require('module').register is 'undefined' in the container and 'function' on host node 24.15.0. material.subject: ENGINE classification, split out of owc-async-context-and-rejections (witness .gm/witness/owc-async-context-and-rejections.txt). AsyncLocalStorage keeps its store across setTimeout, nextTick, setImmediate and promise .then but loses it across every await (await null, await 42, await Promise.resolve(1), await timer promise, two awaits in a row): host Node 24.15 keeps the store in all of them. Measured cause: unlike V8, QuickJS does call Promise.prototype.then for await, but the async-function suspension unwinds the JS stack first, so the guest hook's finally has already restored currentFrame when the engine calls then (frameAtThen=undefined), and the async function's resumption runs in a job of its own enqueued after the reaction returns, so no JS-level reaction wrapper can hand it the frame. guest/loader.ts runInAsyncContext covers only timers, ticks and microtasks; there is no host hook around JS_ExecutePendingJob. Missing hook, named: V8's promise hook (SetPromiseHook with init/before/after/promiseResolve) that Node's async_hooks AsyncLocalStorage is built on; its QuickJS analogue would be a host hook on job enqueue/run. Evidence it is absent: an exhaustive scan of quickjs-emscripten@0.32.0 (18 files, exhaustive: true) holds neither 'setHostPromiseRejectionTracker' nor 'Hook'. Unblocks only by shipping a QuickJS build that exposes a promise/async-context hook (rebuilding the engine to WASM), or by moving the guest off QuickJS await.

material.subject: ENGINE classification, measured while closing owc-async-context-and-rejections (witness .gm/witness/owc-async-context-and-rejections.txt item 4). `(async function () { throw new Error('asyncfn-throw'); })();` with a 20 ms timer after it: host node 24.15 prints the error on stderr and exits 1 without running the timer; the container prints 'end' and exits 0, so the rejection is lost. Cause: the rejection tracker in packages/core/src/process/executors/node/process.ts sees only promises built through its Promise subclass, and QuickJS builds the result of an async function with the intrinsic %Promise%, not through Promise[Symbol.species], so no cell exists for it. Same wall as owc-als-across-await-engine: the missing hook is a host promise-rejection/job hook (JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker, or a job-enqueue hook), and an exhaustive scan of quickjs-emscripten@0.32.0 (18 files, exhaustive: true) holds neither 'setHostPromiseRejectionTracker' nor 'Hook'.

material.commit_comment: commit eadbc9e27a7ad4861350bb4c1c243d13f8a09b8e
material.subject: GOAL (serves owc-stream-readline): programs that require node:stream, node:stream/promises, node:readline and node:readline/promises inside the OWC in-browser runtime behave as Node 24 for the common surface, verified by live runs against real Node 24. MEANS: stream.ts SRC defines BF stream, BF stream/promises, BF readline, BF readline/promises; no other file is edited.
material.witness: 140-case differential against host Node 24.15 (/tmp/owc-dm/tab/main.js, run on host with /tmp/owc-dm/host.mjs and in the container with /tmp/owc-dm/iowc.mts): MATCH 138 DIFFER 2 MISSING 0, exit 0 on both. Fixed in packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/guest/modules/stream.ts: readline/promises Readline is now Node 24's own cursor-control class (cursorTo/moveCursor/clearLine/clearScreenDown chain and queue, commit() answers a promise, rollback() drops, autoCommit writes each on the next tick) instead of an alias of Interface; Readable.toWeb/fromWeb, Writable.toWeb/fromWeb and Duplex.toWeb/fromWeb added; Readable.prototype.iterator/.compose/.wrap added; a terminal Interface now closes on Ctrl-D and raises SIGINT on Ctrl-C; rl.history records the lines read most recent first. The two remaining differences are the escape codes host's terminal readline writes when it echoes a line (cosmetic) and the names of host's own internal Interface methods. An interactive run driven one keystroke at a time over process.stdin matches host line for line.

material.commit_comment: commit ae9784060b6b442becdeaeb089ea83990af7a2e6
material.subject: OWC's Http2Session emits a 'remoteSettings' event that host Node 24.15 does not: with default settings exchanged, host prints only 'localSettings' for both the client and the server session, while the container prints 'localSettings' AND 'remoteSettings' for both. Found by the owc-h2-extra-goaway-event differential (/tmp/owc-r4/goaway/, every scenario in host4.out vs owc4.raw). Decide whether Node suppresses 'remoteSettings' when the peer's SETTINGS carry only defaults, and witness against Node 24.15.
material.witness: Same two probes run under host Node 24.15 and in the container (/tmp/owc-dm/h2/patch.js and patch2.js). With session.emit replaced and no remoteSettings listener attached, neither side raises remoteSettings: host logs connect x2, stream, localSettings x2, close x2 and the container logs the same six. With a remoteSettings listener attached, both sides raise it on both sessions. So host does emit the event; the run that reported otherwise replaced emit and never attached a listener. Fixed the one real difference in packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/guest/modules/http2.ts: remoteSettings is now raised only when the session has a listener, with the SETTINGS ACK still sent first, so the prompt-ACK cases are untouched. The eight-line HTTP/2 witness (/tmp/owc-r4/h2w/main.js) is byte for byte identical on host and in the container after the change.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21 against host Node 24.15 by a fresh verifier. Implemented: -v, --version, -e, --eval, -p, --print. Diverging: `node --help` -> host prints 24382 bytes, exit 0; container 'node: bad option: --help', exit 9. `node --check ok.js` -> host exit 0 silent; container 'node: bad option: --check', exit 9; `node --check bad.js` -> host exit 1 with a SyntaxError dump, container exit 9. `node -pe 1+1` -> host '2' exit 0, container 'bad option: -pe' exit 9. `node --version=x` -> host 'v24.15.0' exit 0, container 'bad option: --version=x' exit 9. `node -- -e` -> host resolves module '-e', container prefixes a slash and resolves '/-e'. `node -e` with no argument and `node -Z` do agree (exit 9, message matches) when run alone.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-22, load 6.7-8.9, free RAM 790-1116 MB. Distinct from owc-shell-set-e-andor (AND-OR list) and owc-shell-set-e-subshell (subshell), which this adjudication did not re-test. The 'sh -c' form is CORRECT: host and container both give stdout '' and exit 1 for 'set -e; false; echo after'. The interactive form diverges. Driving an interactive shell one keystroke at a time: host /bin/sh (bash 3.2.57, real pty) - 'set -e' then 'false' on the next line ends the shell (the pty closes, no further prompt); the container's own sh - 'set -e' then 'false' then 'echo after' - the shell survives and prints 'after', with the exit marker reporting 0. So errexit is dropped once the line comes from the interactive loop rather than from -c. Note the interactive loop also never exits on a bare failing line, so a script pasted or typed into the playground terminal keeps going where bash would stop.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. 16 of 17 END_STREAM sub-cases match (no-body request, empty payloads, zero-length DATA, trailers, endStream:true, GOAWAY). Two diverge. (1) After `res.end('P'); res.stream.close(NGHTTP2_NO_ERROR, cb)` the host client sees 'end:bytes=1' then 'close'; the container client sees the response and then nothing for 1.5s — END_STREAM is swallowed when the server closes with NO_ERROR after end(). (2) On GOAWAY the container emits two extra goaway events whose opaqueData is undefined, and Buffer.from(opaque) throws TypeError there, killing the program.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21, stable 3/3 runs. With a server listening on 127.0.0.1 and a client connecting, the host fires the server's 'connection' handler before the client's connect callback ('srv:conn' then 'cli:connect') and the container fires the client's callback first ('cli:connect' then 'srv:conn'). Every byte, state and count matches; only the accept ordering is inverted, which any program that assumes the server has seen the connection before it writes will notice.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. net.connect({host:'nx-host.invalid', port}) throws synchronously out of the constructor with 'ENOENT: No such file or directory, /etc/hosts' from netResolve, and the process then never exits (the harness watchdog fired at 8s). Host Node delivers an async ENOTFOUND error via getaddrinfo and exits normally. 'localhost' resolves correctly, so only the failure path is wrong; any package that probes a hostname sees a thrown ENOENT and then hangs.

material.witness: adv/c09-net-nxhost (c09/main.mjs) after the fix: stdout, stderr and exit code identical to host Node 24.15 (0/0). The process exits (exit 0); before the fix it threw 'ENOENT: No such file or directory, /etc/hosts' out of the constructor and the runner hit its 15000ms timeout (exit 124). 'localhost' still connects first.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. WebSocket URL handling diverges everywhere: http/https are not coerced to ws/wss (the container throws 'Failed to construct'), every rejection is a plain SyntaxError where the host raises DOMException SyntaxError with a different message, arity is reported as an invalid URL instead of '1 argument required', 'ws://' with no host is accepted, 'ws://x.test' is not normalised to 'ws://x.test/', and an invalid Sec-WebSocket-Protocol value (empty, space, duplicate) is accepted instead of rejected. The frame round trip itself is byte-exact.

material.commit_comment: close already waits for the connection to end; re-measured, no change needed
material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 by an adjudicating verifier on a machine at load 5.5-7.6, free RAM 0.15-2.1 GB, 3 runs per side. A raw net+crypto server performs the handshake, sends a text frame 'hi', then a close frame (0x88 0x02 0x03E8, code 1000). Host Node 24.15 fires open, message, and then NOTHING: readyState stays 2 (CLOSING) for the full 2 s wait. It only fires close (code 1000, wasClean true, a real CloseEvent) after the server closes the socket, at +50 ms after the FIN. The container fires close at +1 ms after the close frame regardless of whether the server ever sends a FIN, with readyState 3. Same shape with 2 s wait and with or without sock.end(). Any program that waits for close before proceeding sees it ~immediately in the container and hangs on the host; conversely a program that expects to stay CLOSING until the peer hangs up diverges.
material.subject: WebSocket: the close event fires on the server's close frame without waiting for the peer to close the TCP connection
material.witness: witness2.sh under session verify-ws-close-before-fin: no-FIN host-exit=0 cont-exit=0 cont-stderr-bytes=0 'WS-CLOSE no-FIN: stdout IDENTICAL'; FIN host-exit=0 cont-exit=0 cont-stderr-bytes=0 'WS-CLOSE FIN: stdout IDENTICAL'; host stderr 0 bytes on both. A raw net+crypto server handshakes, sends text 'hi' then a close frame 1000 and keeps the socket: host and container both stay readyState=2 with events [open,message] for the full 1.8s; with sock.end() both fire close code=1000 reason='' wasClean=true isCloseEvent=true ctor=CloseEvent at readyState=3. Fixed by 9b1d545437b33077c11065da0814d6628fef073a and present at HEAD.
material.witness_plan: Run /tmp/owc-r4/adj/ws/ws2.mjs (and main.mjs) with and without FIN=1; host must stay readyState=2 with no close event until the server closes the socket, and the container must match that.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21 vs host /bin/sh. `sh -c 'set -e; false && echo x; echo alive'` prints 'alive' with exit 0 on the host (POSIX exempts a command that is not the last of an && or || list) and prints nothing with exit 1 in the container. Consequence: any script that guards a failing command with && dies under set -e.
material.subject: shell: set -e wrongly fires on a non-final command of an AND-OR list

bash dispatch 1792651365275-943-4d7b281caa673e6e => 6/6 cases MATCH vs /bin/sh on stdout, stderr and exit code: 'set -e; false && true; echo after' now 'after
' exit 0 (was '' exit 1), 'set -e; false || true; echo after' 'after
' 0, 'set -e; false && echo x; echo alive' 'alive
' 0, 'set -e; ! true; echo after' 'after
' 0; 'set -e; true && false; echo after' still exits 1 as on the host.
material.witness_plan: Run `sh -c 'set -e; false && echo x; echo alive'` on both sides; stdout 'alive', exit 0 on both.

material.description: Differential vs host /bin/sh (macOS bash-as-sh), measured 2026-10-21 by a fresh verifier. `sh -c '(set -e; false; echo no); echo st=$?'` prints 'st=1' on the host (the subshell exits 1 before echo) and 'no\nst=0' in the container: the subshell runs the next command and reports 0. Everything else about subshells matches (grouping, cd scope, exit propagation without set -e). Fix: honour the errexit flag in the subshell's own execution loop, not only in the parent's.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. On the host `sh -c 'node -e; echo E=$?'` prints E=9; in the container it prints E=0, though `node -e` alone does exit 9 on both sides. Same for `node --unknown-flag` and `node -Z`. The exit status of a node invocation is lost as soon as another command follows it on the same line, so scripts that test $? after node never see a failure.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. `chmod -w a` (and the other symbolic forms that name a permission letter without a who, e.g. -r, -x) prints 'chmod: illegal option -- w' plus a BSD usage block in the container and leaves the mode unchanged, while host /bin/sh chmod sets -r--r--r--. The forms that do work are u+x, go-r, a=r, +x, u=rwx,g=rx,o= . POSIX allows the who to be omitted.

Host throws, container accepts: 'trace'/'CONNECT' method, GET with a body, Request with no arguments, a relative or malformed URL, Response statusText with a newline, status 99/600, status 204/205/304 with a body, Request built from an already-used Request. Also Response body is typed 'string' where the host says 'object', and status 200.5 is not truncated to 200.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21 by a fresh verifier. `chmod 000 a` on an existing file: stdout and exit code match, but the container adds stderr 'chmod: a: permissions are not enforced in this container; the file is still readable'. It is not cosmetic: `chmod 000 a; cat a` exits 1 with 'Permission denied' on the host and succeeds in the container. The warning also fires for mode 200 but not 400. Either drop the warning, or enforce the bit.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. Two separate divergences in one area. (1) `chmod 700 link`, link -> target: host chmod follows the link and changes target (ls shows '-rwx------ target'); the container changes the link itself and leaves target untouched. (2) `ls -l` never renders a symlink: host prints 'lrwxr-xr-x 1 link -> target'; the container prints '-rwxr-xr-x 1 link' — no 'l' type character, 755 instead of 777, and no '-> target'. Any package that inspects a tree with links sees a different shape.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21. Bodies are coerced instead of kept as bytes: a Uint8Array body serialises as '1,2,3' (host: 3 bytes), an ArrayBuffer as '[object ArrayBuffer]' (host: 3 bytes), null becomes 'stream' (host: null), and the content-type for a string, Uint8Array or URLSearchParams body is null where the host sets 'text/plain;charset=UTF-8' or 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8'. With FormData only the first entry is serialised and the content-type prefix is empty; an empty FormData serialises as '[object FormData]'; a URLSearchParams built from an array of pairs serialises indices instead of names.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-21 against this host with LANG=en_US.UTF-8. `touch a B; ls` prints 'a' then 'B' on the host (strcoll collation) and 'B' then 'a' in the container (code point order). Under LC_ALL=C the host agrees with the container, so the fix is to honour LC_COLLATE when a locale is set; without it, every listing of mixed-case names differs.

material.commit_comment: stale at HEAD: byte-identical to host
material.description: Measured 2026-10-22, differential vs host Node 24.15 with paced writes (each write waiting for its own callback). The deflate-family -- gzip, deflate, deflate-raw -- COMPRESS STREAMS diverge from Node byte for byte, in two ways the brotli/zstd row did not cover. (1) flush() is a no-op: createGzip() over 5000 bytes gives host 95 bytes unflushed, 158 with a flush between two halves and 101 with a flush after the write, where the container gives 94 for all three; deflate is 83/146/89 vs 82, deflate-raw 77/140/83 vs 76. (2) even with no flush at all the stream is one byte short of Node's: host 95/83/77, container 94/82/76, while the sync forms gzipSync/deflateSync/deflateRawSync of the same 5000 bytes are 95/83/77 and already match. So the stream path loses a byte and the flush does nothing. Cause: those streams buffer every write and run the one-shot fflate call at the end, with ZlibStream.prototype.flush a no-op callback -- a different code path from the wasm codecs brotli and zstd use, which now stream one call at a time. Probe: /tmp/owc-r4/csgz/main.js (host.tsv vs the container run of the same file).
material.subject: gzip/deflate/deflate-raw streams: flush() is a no-op and the stream output is one byte short of Node's

Every length and payload matches: gz 95/158/101, gz9 95/158/101, def 83/146/89, defraw 77/140/83, base64 identical. flush() is not a no-op and the stream is no longer one byte short: the row's premise was fixed before this run and is refuted at HEAD, with no code change.

material.commit_comment: commit c6d7f3c: a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol the client never offered fails the handshake
material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 (adv/ws2 scenario 2, raw RFC6455 server built on node:net). A client that requests subprotocols ['a'] and gets 'Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: zzz' in the 101 response fires 'error' on host Node and never opens, while the container fires 'open' and continues. Negotiating ['a','b'] with 'b' matches on both sides (ws.protocol === 'b'), so only the unrequested-protocol path diverges.
material.subject: WebSocket: a server-selected subprotocol the client did not request is accepted (open) instead of failing the connection
material.witness: Fixed in commit c6d7f3c (handshake check in guest/modules/undici.ts). Live differential /tmp/owc-wslane/probes/wsx/main.mjs, raw net server answers 101 with Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: zzz to a client offering ['a']: host prints 'subproto-bad error ctor=ErrorEvent ... readyState=3', 'subproto-bad close code=1006 ... readyState=3' and no open line; the container now prints the same, and the two further cases also match ('subproto-two' with 'a, b' and 'subproto-case' with 'A' both fail on both sides, 'subproto-ok' with ['a','b'] vs 'b' opens with protocol="b" on both). WSX stdout IDENTICAL, host-exit=0 cont-exit=0 cont-stderr-bytes=0. Before the fix the container printed 'subproto-bad open protocol="zzz"'.
material.witness_plan: With a raw net server answering 101 with an unrequested Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, connect a client requesting ['a'] on both sides; host fires error, the container must too.

material.commit_comment: commit c6d7f3c: socket state behind prototype accessors, EventTarget-shaped base, real MessageEvent
material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 in the container against host Node 24.15, found while closing the WebSocket URL, event, handler and send/close rows; none of them names it. The WebSocket constructor stores url, protocol, extensions, readyState, bufferedAmount and its internals (_socket, _frags, _fragOp, _settled, _closeCode, _closeReason, _closeReceived, _closeReceivedReason) as enumerable own properties, where host Node keeps every attribute as a prototype accessor and an instance has no own properties at all: 'for (const k in ws)' on the host lists [CLOSED, CLOSING, CONNECTING, OPEN, addEventListener, binaryType, bufferedAmount, close, dispatchEvent, extensions, onclose, onerror, onmessage, onopen, protocol, readyState, removeEventListener, send, url] -- the same names the prototype declares -- and in the container adds every _-prefixed field. Related, three more: addEventListener/removeEventListener/dispatchEvent sit on WebSocket.prototype in the container and on EventTarget.prototype in the host, so they are in Object.getOwnPropertyNames(WebSocket.prototype) only on one side; the 'message' event is a hand-built object (own type/data/origin/lastEventId/target) where the host delivers a MessageEvent whose attributes are prototype getters and which also carries source and ports; and the container's URL global is weak enough that a WebSocket URL keeps a raw space, a newline or an IPv6 literal that the host percent-encodes or folds (see owc-url-global-normalisation). Fixing this means moving the per-instance state behind prototype accessors, or at least defining it non-enumerable.
material.subject: WebSocket: an instance exposes its state as enumerable own properties, so for-in and Object.getOwnPropertyNames differ from host Node 24.15
material.witness: Fixed in commit c6d7f3c (state moved into a WeakMap behind prototype accessors, base prototype over EventTarget, MessageEvent in guest/modules/undici.ts). Live differential /tmp/owc-wslane/probes/wss/main.mjs over an open socket, host Node 24.15 vs container, all 17 lines identical: 'for-in ws' = [close,send,readyState,bufferedAmount,url,extensions,protocol,onopen,onerror,onclose,onmessage,binaryType,CONNECTING,OPEN,CLOSING,CLOSED,addEventListener,removeEventListener,dispatchEvent]; 'ownNames ws' = [] (was 22 _-prefixed own properties plus the emitter's three); 'protoNames WebSocket.prototype' = [constructor,close,send,readyState,bufferedAmount,url,extensions,protocol,onopen,onerror,onclose,onmessage,binaryType,CONNECTING,OPEN,CLOSING,CLOSED]; proto-of-proto ctor EventTarget with [constructor,addEventListener,removeEventListener,dispatchEvent]; ws instanceof EventTarget true; toStringTag "WebSocket"; message event ctor MessageEvent, ownNames [], keys [], source=null, ports=[], origin="ws://127.0.0.1:18510" (the url's origin, no path), targetIsWs=true, instanceof MessageEvent and Event true. WSS stdout IDENTICAL, host-exit=0 cont-exit=0 cont-stderr-bytes=0.
material.witness_plan: Differential 'for (const k in ws)', Object.getOwnPropertyNames(ws), Object.getOwnPropertyNames(WebSocket.prototype) and a message event's own keys over an open socket, host Node 24.15 vs container; every line must match.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 (adv/ctl-chmod2 owcm4, owcm5, owcm7; adv/ctl-ls2 owcl4). `chmod 2755 b` on the host fails with 'chmod: Unable to change file mode on b: Operation not permitted' and leaves -rw-r--r--, while the container succeeds and renders -rwxr-sr-x; `chmod 7777 a` gives host exit 1 with the same error and container exit 0 with -rwsrwsrwt. Setuid (4xxx) and sticky (1xxx) match on both; only the setgid bit diverges. The host refusal is an APFS property, so the divergence may be a host artifact - but the exit code differs (1 vs 0), which a package can observe.
material.subject: chmod accepts setgid (2xxx) and 7777 where the host filesystem refuses with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1 vs 0)

material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 against host Node 24.15 and /bin/sh. ZenFSCore.statPath now returns the inode's real `mode` (added so `isexe`, and `which` behind it, can see the executable bit on /usr/local/bin/node), and a guest's `fs.chmodSync('f',0o755); fs.statSync('f').mode` now reports 0755 as host Node does. The shell does not use it: `stat -c %a f.txt` prints `644`, `chmod 755 f.txt; stat -c %a f.txt` still prints `644`, and `ls -l` prints `-rw-r--r--`, because shell/commands/fileutils.ts keeps its own `modes` Map and falls back to DEFAULT_FILE_MODE 0o644 (and DEFAULT_DIR_MODE 0o755) instead of reading the mode the file system reports. The Readme line "chmod and fs.chmodSync succeed and change nothing" is now true only of the shell. Fix: `modeOf(fs, path, fallback)` reads `fs.statPath(path).mode` when the file system gives one, and `chmod` writes through to the file system when it can.

material.commit_comment: fix already present at HEAD: a job is replayed from its source
material.description:
Measured 2026-10-22 against this machine’s /bin/sh (bash 3.2.57). `(echo 'a  b') & wait` is host stdout "a  b
", container "a b
"; `(echo '*') & wait` is host "*
", container the names of the files in the directory; `{ echo 'a  b'; } & wait` is host "a  b
", container "a b
". The same words inline keep their quoting, so only a job loses it. A job stores the words `&` was written with, already through rawText (which takes the quoting out), and replays them -- `job.line === undefined ? shellPipeline(shell, job.stages) : runCompoundJob(shell, job.line)` -- rather than replaying the source. It is also what stops a job’s own EXIT trap from being right: `(trap 'echo inner' EXIT) & wait` runs `trap echo inner EXIT`, whose action is bare `echo`, so the job prints an empty line where the host prints `inner`. Fix site: startBackgroundJob / jobText / runJob in packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/capabilities/child.ts.
material.subject: a background job is replayed from its words, so its quoting is gone: `(echo 'a  b') &` prints `a b`
material.witness:
Container now matches the host on all three cases in .gm/witness-out/owc-shell-background-job-quoting-lost.txt: `(echo 'a  b') & wait` -> "a  b
" both, `(echo '*') & wait` -> "*
" both, `{ echo 'a  b'; } & wait` -> "a  b
" both. The job is replayed from ShellJob.source (packages/core/src/shell/shell.ts), not from the printed words.
